h1: The 6 Best Noise-Canceling Speakerphones for Calls and Small Meetings, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 noise-canceling speakerphones from Jabra, Anker, Yealink and EMEET, compared on mics, certification and battery.
summary: The Anker PowerConf with six microphones and Zoom certification is the best noise-canceling speakerphone for most people. The Jabra Speak2 55 is the premium wireless choice for refined call clarity, the Jabra Speak2 40 is certified for both Zoom and Google Meet, and the Yealink SP92 brings AI noise cancellation and 20 hours of call time at a lower price.
intro: Noise cancellation on a speakerphone is not the same thing as noise cancellation on headphones. Headphones remove sound for the listener. A speakerphone has to clean up sound for the people on the other end, which means separating your voice from keyboard clatter, a fan or the person beside you. How it does that depends on the number and arrangement of microphones, which is why mic count is more telling than a marketing label.

This ranking sorts six speakerphones by microphone design, platform certification, connectivity and battery. Our read of each listing treats sound quality as a function of those features, not as a measurement. Where a listing is generic about its noise handling, we say so, and prices are shown as buckets only.

products.name: Anker PowerConf Speakerphone, Zoom Certified Conference Speaker with 6 Mics
products.verdict: Six microphones, Zoom certification, echo cancellation and background noise reduction.
products.description:
The Anker PowerConf has six microphones, Zoom certification, echo cancellation and background noise reduction, with Bluetooth and USB connection in a compact body. It costs $100 to $200.

A six-mic array lets the unit steer towards a talker and shrink the pickup of side noise, which is the physical basis of noise cancellation. The Zoom certification means it passed the platform's checks for compatibility, and a compact body fits a desk or a small meeting table. It is the strongest mic setup in the group.

Buy it for a home office or a small meeting room. Skip it if you want a premium wireless build.
cons: Not certified for other platforms in the listing
products.idealFor: Zoom-heavy home offices and small rooms.
products.skipIf: You want a premium wireless design.

products.name: Jabra Speak2 55 Wireless Bluetooth Speakerphone (2025 Edition), Dark Grey
products.verdict: A premium wireless Jabra with background noise and echo cancellation and refined build quality.
products.description:
The Jabra Speak2 55 is a 2025 edition wireless Bluetooth speakerphone with background noise and echo cancellation and a premium build. It costs $100 to $200.

It ranks second because Jabra's strength is call clarity and an unfussy, polished design. The listing is brief on mic count, so we cannot compare it with the Anker on hardware, but Jabra is the established name in this category and the unit is compact and wireless. It trades fine detail for brand confidence.

Choose it for polished design and strong support. Skip it if you want listed mic numbers.
products.idealFor: Callers who value polish and support.
products.skipIf: You want mic specs spelled out.

products.name: Jabra Speak2 40 Portable Speakerphone, 4 Noise-Cancelling Mics, Certified for Zoom and Google Meet
products.verdict: Four mics, a 50mm speaker, wideband audio and certification for both Zoom and Google Meet.
products.description:
The Jabra Speak2 40 has four noise-cancelling microphones, a 50mm speaker with wideband audio, and plugs into either USB-A or USB-C. It is certified for Zoom and Google Meet. It costs $100 to $200.

It ranks third because dual certification suits anyone who switches between platforms, and both USB connectors plug into laptops of any age. The 50mm speaker gives full-range sound for calls and light music. It has fewer mics than the Anker, and the listing does not mention Bluetooth, so check the connection options.

Buy it if your meetings span Zoom and Google Meet. Skip it if you need Bluetooth.
products.idealFor: Users who switch between Zoom and Google Meet.

products.name: Yealink SP92 Conference Speaker and Microphone with AI Noise Cancellation, 20H Call Time, 13ft Pick-up, 360 Omni Mic
products.verdict: AI noise cancellation, a 13 ft pickup radius and 20 hours of call time at a lower price.
products.description:
The Yealink SP92 offers AI noise cancellation, a 360 degree omni microphone with a 13 ft pickup radius, a 50mm full-duplex speaker, Bluetooth 5.3 and 20 hours of call time, with USB and Bluetooth connections. It costs $50 to $100.

It ranks fourth because the specification is generous for the price: explicit AI noise cancellation, long battery life and a wide pickup. Full-duplex lets both sides speak at once without cutting each other off. Yealink is better known in conference systems than consumer audio, so its listing is more technical than rivals. It does not list a Zoom certification.

Choose it for a long day of calls on a budget. Skip it if platform certification matters.
products.idealFor: Long call days on a budget.

products.name: EMEET M0 Plus Conference Speaker and Microphone, 4 Mics 360 degrees Voice Pickup
products.verdict: A compact four-mic, 360 degree conference speaker with USB and Bluetooth.
products.description:
The EMEET M0 Plus has four microphones with 360 degree voice pickup, USB and Bluetooth connections and a compact body. It costs $50 to $100.

It ranks fifth because it delivers the core of a good speakerphone at a low price, with four mics and both connection types. The listing offers no battery life, certification or noise algorithm name, which puts it below the Yealink on stated features.

Buy it as a budget all-rounder. Skip it if you want listed battery life.
products.skipIf: You want a stated battery life.

products.name: Jabra Speak 510 (2025 Edition) Portable USB Bluetooth Speaker, Black
products.verdict: A compact, travel-friendly Jabra with background noise reduction, USB and Bluetooth.
products.description:
The Jabra Speak 510 2025 edition is a portable USB and Bluetooth speakerphone with background noise reduction and a compact, travel-friendly body. It costs $50 to $100.

It ranks last because it is the plainest of the three Jabra models, with only noise reduction named and no mic count. Its value is portability and the Jabra name, so it is an easy fit for a desk that doubles as a meeting spot or a trip bag.

Buy it for travel and light meetings. Skip it if you want echo cancellation spelled out.

whatMatters.detail: More microphones let the unit focus on voices and reject side noise. A 360 degree array covers a table. Look for a mic count and a pickup radius on the listing.
Full-duplex means both sides can talk at once without one cutting out the other. It matters in conversations. Look for full-duplex in the specifications.
Without it, the person you are speaking to hears themselves. It is vital for a speakerphone. Check that the listing names echo cancellation.
Zoom or Teams certification means the maker has tested the unit with the platform. It reduces compatibility surprises. Check the platforms you use.
USB suits a desk, and Bluetooth suits a phone. A stated call time, such as 20 hours, tells you how long it lasts untethered.

cards.text: Strong noise reduction, a tight pickup and a moderate volume. Avoid a 360 degree pickup that records neighbours.

cards.text: The Anker PowerConf with six mics isolates voices best, and the Jabra Speak2 55 offers polished background noise cancellation.

faq.q: Can a speakerphone replace a headset?
faq.a: For group calls, yes. For private calls or noisy rooms, a headset is better. A speakerphone suits a desk where others are present.
Placing it near a keyboard or a monitor fan. Put it close to the speakers, away from noise sources, and about an arm's length from talkers.

faq.q: Is the Anker worth it over the Yealink?
faq.a: For voice isolation and Zoom compatibility, yes. For battery life and price, the Yealink is hard to beat.
Plug in the USB cable or pair over Bluetooth. Select the device as your speaker and microphone in your call app.
Wipe the mic ports with a dry cloth, charge the battery regularly and update firmware through the maker's app if available.

faq.q: Does noise cancellation work for the listener too?
faq.a: It cleans the sound you send, not the sound you hear. Background noise in your room is reduced for other participants.

finalTake: The Anker PowerConf with six mics and Zoom certification is the best noise-canceling speakerphone for most people. The Jabra Speak2 55 is the polished wireless pick, the Speak2 40 covers both Zoom and Google Meet, and the Yealink SP92 offers AI noise cancellation and 20 hours of call time for less. Choose by your meeting platform and room size.
